learning_outcomes.text: Possess the ability to design, develop, implement, manage and improve products, systems and processes in different industrial fields, using appropriate analytical, computational or experimental techniques.
Apply the acquired knowledge to identify, formulate and solve problems in broad contexts, being able to integrate them working in multidisciplinary teams.
Understand the impact of engineering on the environment, the sustainable development of society and the importance of working in a professional and responsible environment.
Possess learning skills that allow continuous lifelong learning for adequate professional development.
Incorporate ICT and industrial engineering technologies and tools into their professional activities.
Knowledge and capabilities for the calculation, design and testing of machines.
Knowledge and capabilities for the design of machine elements.

syllabus_topics: Chapter I Stresses in Machine Elements
Topic 1: Analysis of loads and stresses.
Concept of failure and factor of safety.
Topic 3: Fatigue failure under variable loads.
Chapter II Design of non-permanent joints
Threaded fasteners. Joint stiffness and bolt preloading.
Bolt strength in tension joints. Fatigue of tension joints.
Joints subjected to bending and/or shear.
Chapter III Design of permanent joints
Fit in cylinders: hub and shaft. Transmitted torque.
assessment_rules: The final grade in the ordinary call (C) is the maximum of the progressive evaluation (C_PROG) and the global evaluation (C_ORD), requiring a minimum of 5 to pass. For C_PROG, the formula is 0.45*PROG1 + 0.45*ORD2 + 0.10*LAB, with a minimum of 4 in PROG1 and ORD2, and attendance/submission for LAB; C_PROG is capped at 4 if conditions are not met. For C_ORD, the formula is 0.45*max(PROG1,ORD1) + 0.45*ORD2 + 0.10*max(LAB,ORD3), requiring a minimum of 4 in either PROG1 or ORD1, 4 in ORD2, and 4 in ORD3 or successful LAB completion; C_ORD is capped at 4 if conditions are not met. The extraordinary call consists of a single 100% written exam, requiring a minimum score of 5 to pass.
